title: ppx_jane derivers: sexp, compare, equal, hash
body: A PPX is a compile-time rewriter. Writing `type t = { major : int; minor : int; patch : int } [@@deriving sexp, compare, equal, hash]` asks the `ppx_jane` bundle to generate `sexp_of_t`, `t_of_sexp`, `compare`, `equal` and `hash_fold_t`/`hash` from the type definition. You write the type once, and the boilerplate can never drift out of date.

Derived functions compose. Because every field type has its own derived functions, a record of records gets structural versions of all of them, and `[%sexp (x : t)]` converts a value to an s-expression inline. S-expressions are Jane Street's universal text format for config files, debug output and expect tests.

`Comparable.Make (T)` then adds `<`, `>`, `max`, `min`, `ascending` and friends on top of a `compare` and `sexp_of_t`, so you get readable operators without shadowing polymorphic comparison. Derive only what you use: each deriver adds code and compile time.
challenge: Version.t is a plain record with stub functions. Derive sexp, compare, equal and hash for it, include `Comparable.Make`, and implement `of_string` for "major.minor.patch" (all three parts must be non-negative integers) and `bump_minor` (increment minor, reset patch to 0).
projectInstructions: Run `dune test --root .`. The first failure is a compile error because the derived functions do not exist yet. Edit only src/version.ml.
question: What does `[@@deriving compare]` generate?
correct: A structural compare function for the type, built from the compare functions of its fields
wrong: A runtime check that the type is sorted
A copy of the type in another module
reasoning: Derivers read the type definition at compile time and emit the corresponding functions, so they stay in sync with the type.
